what: Johnson Controls makes building systems: heating and cooling equipment, chillers for data centres and large buildings, fire detection and suppression, security systems, and the software that ties them together.
customers: Owners and operators of commercial buildings, data centres, hospitals, schools and industrial plants.
money: HVAC equipment, fire and security systems, installation and service by region
equipment sold through distributors and contractors
moat: Equipment installed in buildings that need parts and servicing for twenty years, and systems that must be certified and maintained by approved technicians.
risks: It has lagged peers on margins and has been restructuring for years
Commercial construction follows the economic cycle
Selling its residential HVAC joint venture removed a profitable business
Execution under new management still has to be proved
opportunities: Data centre cooling is a large and fast-growing market for its chillers
Service contracts on installed equipment are recurring and higher margin
A simpler portfolio focused on commercial buildings should lift margins toward peers
watch: Organic order growth and the service backlog, plus margin progress against Trane and Carrier.
